candidates.title: Multi-OS deployment
candidates.statement: The system shall be deployable and operable on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 5 and on Solaris 10 running on SPARC hardware.
candidates.source_quote: any reporting system needs to work on both Linux and Solaris

candidates.title: PostgreSQL compatibility
candidates.statement: The system shall be compatible with PostgreSQL (current environment: PostgreSQL 8.3) and operate against a fully relational database schema.
candidates.source_quote: It runs PostgreSQL 8.3 for the database.

candidates.title: Relational-query support
candidates.statement: The system shall support complex joins and queries against the main relational database structure without requiring denormalized reporting schemas.
candidates.source_quote: The reporting system needs to work with the relational structure, not fight against it.
candidates.priority_signals: preference expressed to avoid denormalized schemas; sync issues noted

candidates.title: Background report processing
candidates.statement: The system shall support queuing and background processing of complex reports so that report execution does not directly block interactive operations.
candidates.source_quote: we need to make sure reports can be queued and processed in the background
candidates.priority_signals: "major concern" about tying up the database

candidates.title: Read-only reporting replicas
candidates.statement: The system shall support the use of read-only reporting replicas for running reports to avoid impacting the production database.
candidates.source_quote: Or we need read-only reporting replicas.

candidates.title: Operational-hour performance
candidates.statement: The system shall ensure that searches and reports can be processed during open hours without disrupting other system functions (e.g., circulation, OPAC responsiveness).
candidates.source_quote: The key requirement is that searches and reports can be processed during open hours without disrupting other system functions.

candidates.title: Browser support
candidates.statement: The system shall support Microsoft Internet Explorer 6.0 and later and Mozilla Firefox 2.0 and later for client access.
candidates.source_quote: So we need to support IE 6.0+ and Firefox 2.0+.
candidates.priority_signals: IE6 still common; upgrading 200+ computers is expensive

candidates.title: Section 508 compliance
candidates.statement: The system shall comply with Section 508 accessibility requirements.
candidates.source_quote: we MUST comply with Section 508 accessibility requirements.

candidates.title: Screen reader compatibility
candidates.statement: The system shall be usable with screen readers, including JAWS and NVDA.
candidates.source_quote: Screen readers like JAWS and NVDA

candidates.title: Screen magnifier support
candidates.statement: The system shall be compatible with screen magnification software such as ZoomText.
candidates.source_quote: Screen magnification software like ZoomText

candidates.title: Assistive technology support
candidates.statement: The system shall work with other assistive technology programs used by staff and patrons.
candidates.source_quote: Other assistive technology programs

candidates.title: Standards-compliant HTML output
candidates.statement: The system shall produce standards-compliant HTML output with proper semantic structure, including alt attributes and ARIA labels where appropriate.
candidates.source_quote: The HTML output needs to be properly structured with alt tags, ARIA labels, and proper semantic HTML.

candidates.title: Role-based access control
candidates.statement: The system shall implement role-based access control supporting at least these roles: Patron, Staff, Local Admin, and Global Admin.
candidates.source_quote: PINES uses a role-based system. We have different levels of access: Patron, Staff, Local Admin, Global Admin
candidates.priority_signals: role-based access control is confirmed as essential

candidates.title: Local Admin capabilities
candidates.statement: The system shall allow Local Admin (branch manager) role to run reports and configure local settings.
candidates.source_quote: Local Admin (branch manager - can run reports, configure local settings)

candidates.title: Global Admin capabilities
candidates.statement: The system shall allow Global Admin (IT staff) role to have full system access.
candidates.source_quote: Global Admin (IT staff - full system access)

candidates.title: Security groups/roles integration
candidates.statement: The permission system shall be controllable through security groups and/or roles and integrate with existing group management mechanisms.
candidates.source_quote: The permission system needs to be controlled through security groups and/or "roles."

candidates.title: Granular access control
candidates.statement: The system shall allow access control to be assigned to individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups.
candidates.source_quote: This allows access control for individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups.

candidates.title: Simple role administration
candidates.statement: The system shall make role administration simple and allow changing a user's permissions by changing their role assignment.
candidates.source_quote: Changing someone's permissions should be a simple matter of changing their role assignment.

candidates.title: Developer test environment
candidates.statement: The system shall provide a separate development/test environment where developers can test new reports without affecting production.
candidates.source_quote: Developers need a place to test new reports without affecting production.

candidates.title: Training environment
candidates.statement: The system shall provide a separate training environment where new staff can practice running reports without affecting production data.
candidates.source_quote: new staff members need a training environment where they can practice running reports without worrying about making mistakes.

candidates.title: Export/import migration
candidates.statement: The system shall provide export/import functionality for report templates, permission settings, and other configuration so configurations developed in training/dev can be migrated to production.
candidates.source_quote: We need export/import functionality for report templates, permission settings, and other configuration.
candidates.priority_signals: "key is that configurations developed in training/dev need to be migratable to production"

candidates.title: OPAC isolation
candidates.statement: The reporting system shall be architected so that it does not constrain or slow down the OPAC; heavy reporting queries must not degrade catalog responsiveness for patrons.
candidates.source_quote: The management reporting system must not constrain the OPAC in any way.
candidates.priority_signals: "critical" separation of concerns noted in interviewer's notes

candidates.title: Online hierarchical help
candidates.statement: The system shall provide an online help system that is hierarchical, cross-linked, searchable, and easy to navigate.
candidates.source_quote: the help system needs to be online, hierarchical, and cross-linked... The HTML help needs to be searchable and easy to navigate.
candidates.priority_signals: Staff shouldn't have to call IT every time they want to know how to run a report.
